Section 3.1 prints cross_val_score values only for the iris data loaded from scikit-learn (the data itself is not printed) with its own splits, so no printed value can be reproduced by running G6's cross_validate on printed inputs; the rule is a procedure (fit on k-1 folds of the training part, score the remaining one, the held-out rows never read), and the held-out rows reach the child only as unlabelled features used after the choice.

_caution is a pure string builder: it reads the count and returns text, saying 'optimistic' once the count is 1 or more; it writes nothing and gates nothing. The recording of each scoring (held_out_use, a small SQLite write under G6_HOME) is in another function the certificate's cases do not run; it is declared in the rule and its docstring says it is never a gate.

compare() sets clearly_better true only when the lift's lower end is above zero and adds a note when the score is undefined or too few resamples are defined; the red card for 'does not clearly beat' is chosen by said(), not here. compare() also computes the headline numbers (held_out, baseline, lift, gap), which are not part of this rule and rest on the metric rules.
_leakage_findings only builds a list of findings (copy, correlation, single-feature); prepare() turns a non-empty list into the LEAKAGE refusal. It changes no row, feature or score.

prepare() only refuses (seed, bounds, columns, class thinness, held-out size, class on both sides, duplicates, leakage) or returns the split, evidence and class balance; the refusals not named in this rule (seed, columns, duplicates across the split) are separate refusals, none lowers or changes a result.

_gap_note is a pure function: it returns an extra sentence when the gap is 0.10 or more and the headline is higher-is-better, and an empty string otherwise; it refuses, scores and picks nothing. The refusal (_too_good) and the card now stay in said(), outside the checked function.

The only printed values in 12.2 (0.76, 0.5, 0.43) come from SelectKBest and HistGradientBoostingClassifier on seeded random data split by train_test_split; G6's pipeline has no feature-selection step, imputes, scales and one-hot encodes, and splits by row hash, so no printed value is something G6's _pipeline can be run to reproduce or contradict.

Section 3.1 prints no value for a search over settings: its printed numbers are cross_val_score results for iris loaded from scikit-learn and a split from train_test_split, neither reproducible by running G6's search on printed inputs, and the page does not describe a FLAML search; the rule is a procedure (candidates compared by k-fold on the training part only, the held-out rows scoring the chosen one once).

The one printed value (0.84 in 12.3.3.1) comes from make_classification and train_test_split sharing one RandomState instance across calls; G6 passes an integer to each object and splits by hash, so no printed value is something G6's _estimator can be run to reproduce.
_too_good returns nothing or raises the LEAKAGE MLError carrying the evidence; it computes nothing and changes no value.

not_checked: Issuer state qualified-draft: these checks were frozen after the code they check existed (a retrofit), so by the issuer's freeze rule they can reach qualified-draft at most. A named gap holds it at qualified-draft at most: a threshold these rules apply is G6's own choice, which no source sets: headline_imbalance, preprocessing_in_pipeline. A second route and invariants check these rules, and no value their source prints, by the independent reader's attestation (property-checked, no printed value: balanced_accuracy, baseline, cv_training_part, grouped_hold_out, headline_imbalance, preprocessing_in_pipeline, search_training_part, seed).

These inputs are the ml kernel's, shared with adapt_sklearn (checks.json inherits its certificate folder, bound by the SHA-256 of its inputs); this certificate covers them on adapt_automl's own artifact, and adds the search.

held_out checks printed sample counts on distinct row indices, not an iris model score. stratified applies the printed first-fold counts as a one-third hold-out; it does not claim the identical random split. grouped checks the printed test folds (sorted, and in the printed order at seed 0, where G6's seeded shuffle deals them so), and the case author's reading of them; grouped_hold_out checks the hold-out split's keeping of identical rows on one side.

Property-checked, because the source prints no worked value G6's functions can be run on: search_training_part calls FLAML's search() directly with one fixed dummy-regressor candidate, one trial and no search dimensions, twice with different held-out rows, comparing its training-fold scores with an independent fold mean absolute error and checking that the held-out rows change none of them. cv_training_part is checked through the rank path on cross_validate, the function the search calls for every trial. preprocessing_in_pipeline fits through _fit.fit_predict (the search's final refit) twice with different held-out rows and compares the fitted transformation of the training rows. seed checks the integer random_state passed to an actual G6-created decision tree. baseline compares majority and mean predictions: the source prints 0.579, its most-frequent baseline's score, for a split of the bundled iris data whose labels it does not print, so there is no printed value G6's baseline function can be run on. balanced_accuracy and headline_imbalance compare independent computations; the 10% headline threshold is G6's own choice (headline_imbalance is marked own_choice, which holds this certificate at qualified-draft).

The source's caveat that an integer seed 'may lead to less robust cross-validation results' (12.3.3.2) is not checked, and the results do not say so, though it matters most here: the search compares settings under one integer random_state.

rmse is squared for the printed mean squared error and compared directly with an independent square root on generated inputs. The constant-target R2 case checks only that R2 is reported undefined; generated and boundary inputs include constant non-integer targets.

Each guard fires at its threshold, holds just inside it and fires on its recall set; G6's removal of it breaks its firing case, and a seeded change of its threshold or of a comparison at it is caught. What else its code does rests on the independent reader's word (effect_only). Their thresholds are G6's own. Of interval, only the claim it gates is checked, not the interval's own values. held_out_from_rows checks the caution made from a count, not the count kept under G6_HOME.

Competitive search, budget exhaustion and the equal shares of the trial cap and time budget between several candidates, all search spaces, the block's search orchestration, child_main file transport and the backend's further-process launch remain outside scope; so do the caller rules search_bounds and limits (the typed input's ranges and the process deadline), categorical one-hot encoding and its 50-category cap, all estimator classes and model-selection quality.

accuracy.rule: accuracy: the share of predictions equal to the true class

balanced_accuracy.rule: balanced accuracy: the mean over classes of the share of each class predicted as itself

baseline.rule: a baseline that ignores the features (the most frequent training class, or the mean training target) is scored on the same held-out rows; a tie between classes goes to the first label in text order (G6's own; the source is silent on ties)

bounds.rule: a request is refused before anything is prepared when a row has a column that is neither the target nor a feature, a text cell holds more than 10,000 characters, the text cells hold more than 5,000,000 characters in all, or a classification target has more than 100 classes; the rows to predict are held to the same column and text limits

cv_training_part.rule: candidates are compared by k-fold cross-validation inside the training part only; the held-out rows score the chosen candidate once and choose nothing

grouped.rule: rows with identical features form one group and stay on one side of every fold (G6's grouping of identical rows; the source groups dependent samples), the folds dealt in an order the seed shuffles

grouped_hold_out.rule: rows with identical features also stay on one side of the hold-out split, so no held-out row repeats a training row (G6's grouping of identical rows; the source groups dependent samples)

headline_imbalance.rule: the headline is balanced accuracy when the smallest class holds under 10% of the training rows (a threshold of G6's own; the held-out labels choose nothing), accuracy otherwise; both are always reported

held_out.rule: a score is measured on rows held out of training, which the extension chooses itself from the rows' own hash, so the same rows always give the same held-out rows whatever the seed

held_out_from_rows.rule: each scoring of a held-out set is recorded by its hash, and every scored reply says how many times it was scored before; once a set has been scored before, the reply says a result kept after several tries on it is optimistic

interval.rule: the model is said to beat the baseline only when the lower end of the lift's 95% percentile interval is above zero; the interval comes from 1,000 seeded resamples of the held-out rows by group (rows with identical features drawn together: a cluster bootstrap), fewer when resamples times held-out rows would pass 5,000,000, as the interval says; otherwise the result says the model does not clearly beat the baseline

leakage_probes.rule: a feature equal to the target, with Pearson or Spearman |r| of 0.99 or more against a numeric target (or a two-class numeric classification target) on the training rows, or predicting it alone for every row from the others (leave-one-out) at 0.99 or better and above a baseline, is refused as a suspected leak; the probes need at least 5 rows (10 for the one-feature probe) before they find anything (thresholds of G6's own)

limits.rule: the other sizes and limits one request may carry are the caller's within the typed input's ranges (20,000 rows, 200 features, 1,000 rows to predict, a fit deadline timeout_s of at most 600 s, each estimator's parameters within their ranges), refused beyond them before anything is prepared; the fit's process is stopped at its deadline and its memory capped at 1,536 MB

min_held_out.rule: fewer than 10 independent held-out rows (rows with identical features count once), a class missing from either side of the split, or a class with fewer than 2 distinct rows, is refused

overfit_gap.rule: the train score less the held-out score is reported; a gap of 0.10 or more (rounded to 6 places) adds a note

preprocessing_in_pipeline.rule: imputation, standard scaling (only for estimators flagged scale) and one-hot encoding (at most 50 categories a column, the rarer ones grouped as infrequent: G6's own cap) are fitted on training rows only, as steps of one pipeline, also inside each fold

r2.rule: R squared: one less the residual over the total sum of squares about the mean; undefined, and reported so, when the held-out targets are all equal (the original definition, not a forced finite value)

rmse.rule: root mean squared error, in the target's units

search_bounds.rule: a search's trial cap (at most 200) and time budget (at most 300 s) are the caller's, refused beyond them by the typed input; the search's process is stopped at 1.5 times the budget plus 60 s, and the result says what ended it

search_training_part.rule: a search compares settings by k-fold cross-validation inside the training part only, with the family's pipeline and folds and an equal share of the trial cap and of the time budget for each candidate; the held-out rows score the chosen setting once and choose nothing

seed.rule: one integer seed sets the folds, the resamples and every estimator that takes a random_state; it does not choose the held-out rows

stratified.rule: for classification each class keeps its share of the rows on both sides of the split

too_good.rule: a held-out headline of 0.99 or more, once rounded to 6 places as it is reported, is refused as a suspected leak the features carry between them (a total and its parts), which the one-feature probes cannot see; it is never reported as a measurement (a threshold of G6's own)
